did: Asks can now be checklists as well as decisions: steps only you can take, like setting up a key, each with where to do it and what to paste back. A new Asks page on the home network's web app lists every open ask. You tick off steps or choose an option there, and one button copies a receipt to paste into a session. What you paste stays in that browser tab and is blanked of anything that looks like a key or password. Asks are gone from the phone, along with answering one by voice. The weekly call still reads every ask of both kinds.

calls.title: Where checklists live
options: GitHub's own task lists on the issue
a self-hosted checklist tool on home
a second kind of ask, on a private web page with a receipt
calls.why: Ticking or pasting on GitHub would publish it, and a tool on home would keep a second copy of every ask in step with its issue. Asks already held what waits on you, so a checklist became one more kind of ask.
calls.undo: Drop the checklist kind and the Asks page, and file checklists as prose again.

calls.title: How long the page keeps what you paste
options: only in that browser tab, blanked first
in the browser until the ask closes
on home with your other records
calls.why: A pasted log can carry a secret, and its only destination is a session you copy it to, so it stays no longer than the tab.
calls.undo: Keep receipts in the browser's lasting storage instead.

calls.title: What leaves the phone with asks
options: the pages and voice answers, keeping the routine's filing of old answers
calls.why: An answer already on home would otherwise never be filed. The filing goes once none is left (#3428).
calls.undo: Restore Studio's Asks pages from git.

left: Turning #3423 into the first checklist waits until #3429 merges.
Retiring the routine's filing of old spoken answers waits on home holding none unfiled (#3428).
Blanking is a net: a secret nested three levels deep in quotes, a short lowercase password written in prose, and the second of two AWS keys run together in one pass can still get through.
